meta.title: Evidence of anticipatory forest use behaviours under policy introduction: a systematic map protocol

primary.text: What is the state of the evidence on anticipatory forest use behaviours in the context of policy introduction?
primary.scope: Global forests; policies at global, national or sub-national level that prompt anticipatory forest use behaviours; no date restriction; English-language articles only.

method.approach: Systematic map following CEE guidance and ROSES reporting standards, with two complementary search strategies and a population-intervention-outcome frame.
sources: Four bibliographic databases and two dissertation platforms, searched with a string tested before submission
Backward and forward citation chasing from a 24-article benchmark
method.procedure: Run the search string; deduplicate and screen titles and abstracts in Rayyan; double-screen a random 10 per cent until Cohen's kappa reaches 0.6; screen full texts against population, intervention and outcome criteria; code study, policy, behaviour and context variables; synthesise narratively with a ROSES flow diagram, an EviAtlas world map, heatmaps and an online dataset.
validity_conditions: The search string was tested before submission and the combined strategies retrieved 20 of the 24 benchmark articles
A random 10 per cent of records is double-screened until kappa reaches 0.6 at each stage
No reviewer screens or codes an article they authored
limits: No study design is excluded, so the map describes evidence rather than appraising it

warrant.gap_statement: No systematic evidence synthesis has been conducted on anticipatory forest use behaviours, so their extent and sectoral scope are unknown.
evidence: Ahmad and Xiao, Journal of Policy Modeling, 2013
Pfaff and Robalino, Annual Review of Resource Economics, 2017
CEE systematic map protocol, Environmental Evidence, 2023
